title: Thrift Sherpa: guided batching and quantization calibrator
author: Priya Natarajan
release_notes: Introduce 'Thrift Sherpa' — an offline-guided calibrator that synthesizes workload traces to recommend per-model batching shapes and quantization presets, plus a safe gradual rollout plan. Improves unit token cost for common chat/complete workloads and provides conservative fallbacks for latency-sensitive routes.
description: Context: customers require lower per-token cost without sacrificing tail latency or regressions in output quality. Existing autotuners either over-aggressively quantize or recommend batch sizes that increase p95 for small requests. This PR introduces 'Thrift Sherpa', a guided calibrator that combines sampled production traces, a lightweight simulator of RTT and KV-cache hit rates, and a conservative cost model to propose batching shapes and quant profiles per model + route. Design summary: 1) Offline trace ingestion: a small trace extractor that samples token lengths, sequence distributions, and route metadata. 2) Workload simulator: fast heuristics to estimate batching throughput, p50/p95, and token-level cost under candidate batch shapes and quant profiles. 3) Scoring and constraints: multi-objective score (cost reduction weighted vs. latency SLO and quality delta budget) with hard constraints for routes tagged latency-sensitive. 4) Output: compact JSON recommendation bundle per model with ranked presets and a 'cautious' fallback. 5) Rollout helper: a manifest and a canary runner that performs step-rollouts with automatic rollback on regressions. This change touches the calibrator and the recommendations API; it does not change runtime serving kernels. Motivation: provide a middle ground between one-size-fits-all defaults and full manual profiling; enable product teams to safely adopt quantization and batching with measurable unit economics. Validation: synthetic replay of five representative customers plus two internal workloads; automated regression tests for the scoring function; A/B canary run in perf-canary for 72h with telemetry hooks. Checklist: - [x] trace extractor + schema - [x] simulator with KV/hit heuristics - [x] scoring engine and constraint enforcement - [x] recommendation manifest format and exporter - [x] unit tests and property tests for scoring bounds - [x] integration test with recommendations API - [x] perf-canary run and rollback criteria defined - [x] docs (internal guide + quickstart). Related: ENG-1182 for batching improvements, ENG-1247 for quant presets. Rollout: canary on non-critical tenants for 1 week, then staged release with telemetry gating to 0.5->1->2->5% traffic. Links: Linear ENG-1182 (design), perf-canary dashboard (internal link), design doc in docs/experimental/thrift-sherpa.md.
